flags.title: ARHOME (Private Option) — Expanded But Private Insurance Model
flags.summary: Arkansas expanded Medicaid via 'Private Option' — now ARHOME. Adults 19-64 below 138% FPL enrolled in private marketplace plans with Medicaid funding. Functions differently from standard Medicaid — verify network adequacy. Plans: Arkansas Blue Cross, Ambetter. Apply: access.arkansas.gov. Phone: 888-987-1200.

flags.title: UI 16 Weeks Maximum — Shortest Duration in Entire Registry
flags.summary: Arkansas UI maximum duration is 16 weeks — the absolute shortest in the registry. Max benefit: $451/week. Appeal deadline: 20 days. Route to emergency food, SNAP, and energy assistance PROACTIVELY when UI is filed, not when it runs out. ADWS: 501-682-2121 / dws.arkansas.gov.

flags.title: TANF (TEA) $204/Month, 24-Month State Limit — Near Bottom of Registry
flags.summary: Arkansas TANF (TEA) pays $204/month for family of 3 — near bottom of registry. 24-month STATE lifetime limit (shorter than federal 60-month). Work requirement strictly enforced. Pair with SNAP, ARHOME, child care (CAPS), LIHEAP, food banks.

flags.title: Northwest Arkansas Poultry / Latino Workforce — Tyson Corridor
flags.summary: Bentonville-Fayetteville-Springdale-Rogers metro has highest Latino concentration in AR (~30%+ of Springdale) working in Tyson Foods and poultry processing. Key issues: wage theft, workers comp, OSHA violations, housing cost pressure from Walmart/tech growth. COMPIE: 479-316-0050. CALS Fayetteville: 479-442-0600.

flags.title: Marshallese Community — Springdale, Largest Outside Pacific Islands
flags.summary: Springdale has the largest Marshallese population outside the Marshall Islands (15,000+). COFA migrants have unique federal benefit eligibility — were excluded from Medicaid until 2020 fix; verify current eligibility. COMPIE: 479-316-0050.

flags.title: Arkansas Delta — Concentrated Rural Black Poverty, Limited Services
flags.summary: East Arkansas Delta counties (Phillips, St. Francis, Crittenden, Lee, Monroe, Desha, Chicot, Jefferson) mirror Mississippi Delta in poverty, health disparities, and service scarcity. Legal Aid of Arkansas (Jonesboro): 870-932-5765. Delta AHEC: 870-738-3804. Assume limited digital access.

flags.title: 3-Day Eviction Notice — Fastest Timeline in Registry
flags.summary: Arkansas Residential Landlord-Tenant Act (Ark. Code §18-16-101): 3-day written notice for nonpayment. Unlawful detainer hearing can be within 5 days of filing. Contact legal aid SAME DAY as any notice. CALS: 501-376-3423. Legal Aid AR: 870-932-5765.

flags.title: No State LGBTQ+ Protection — EEOC Only, State Preempts Local Ordinances
flags.summary: Arkansas does not protect sexual orientation or gender identity in state law. Has passed legislation limiting local nondiscrimination ordinances. All LGBTQ+ employment discrimination must route through federal EEOC only. EEOC Little Rock: 501-324-5060.

flags.title: Involuntary Hold: Arkansas Emergency Admission
flags.message: AR involuntary psychiatric hold law: Arkansas Emergency Admission. Statutory authority: Ark. Code § 20-47-210. Maximum initial hold duration: 72 hours. Legal standard: danger to self/others or gravely disabled. A hearing must be held before the hold can be extended. The person has the right to counsel at the hearing.
action_items: Verify hold did not exceed 72 hours without court order
Confirm hearing was held within statutory timeframe
Check that patient rights notice was provided at admission
Request complete hold documentation from facility

flags.title: Psychiatric Patient Rights
flags.message: Psychiatric patients in AR retain fundamental rights during hospitalization: right to communicate with persons outside the facility, right to receive and send mail, right to access legal counsel, right to refuse treatment (with limited exceptions), right to informed consent, right to access medical records, and right to file grievances. These rights cannot be restricted as a condition of treatment.
action_items: Verify patient rights notice was provided and signed
Check whether any rights were restricted and if proper procedures were followed
Confirm access to legal counsel was not impeded

flags.title: Federal Restraint & Seclusion Limits
flags.message: Federal law (42 CFR § 482.13) sets strict limits on restraint and seclusion in AR: physician order required within 1 hour, face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, continuous monitoring required, maximum 4 hours per order for adults (2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under 9), and restraint may only be used to protect the patient from harm — never as punishment, convenience, or retaliation.
action_items: Request restraint/seclusion logs for all episodes
Verify physician order was obtained within 1 hour
Check that face-to-face evaluation occurred within 1 hour
Verify restraint was not used as punishment or convenience
Check for injuries during restraint episodes
legal_references: CMS State Operations Manual Appendix A

flags.title: Involuntary Psychiatric Hold Statute
flags.message: This state has specific statutes governing involuntary psychiatric holds. Know the time limits, hearing rights, and appeal procedures before they expire.

flags.title: Mental Health Patient Bill of Rights
flags.message: This state has a Patient Bill of Rights for mental health facilities. Facilities must inform patients of these rights upon admission.
flags.statute: Arkansas Mental Health Patient Rights Act

flags.title: Discharge Planning Requirements
flags.message: This state requires facilities to create discharge plans with follow-up appointments, medication management, and community resource referrals.
flags.statute: Arkansas Mental Health Discharge Planning Standards
